Você é especialista em Moodle escrevendo uma base de conhecimento em PORTUGUÊS DO BRASIL para o assistente "Darcy" (suporte do AVA da UnB). Pesquise a documentação OFICIAL (docs.moodle.org, versão estável /en/) e destile os tópicos abaixo.

Para CADA tópico, produza um objeto JSON com os campos:
- id: slug kebab-case único
- title: título em PT-BR
- audience: "professor"
- keywords: 8–15 gatilhos em minúsculas (PT com/sem acento, sinônimos, termo em inglês, fragmento de caminho ex.: "/question/bank", "/grade/edit")
- doc: URL REAL oficial (https://docs.moodle.org/en/<Pagina>), VERIFICADA com WebFetch
- body: PT-BR prático — o que é, ONDE clicar (rótulos reais pt_br), tarefas comuns, erros/dicas. 6–14 linhas curtas, \n entre linhas, máx ~120 palavras.

REGRAS:
- Moodle GENÉRICO (não invente coisas da UnB). Rótulos pt_br padrão. Verifique TODAS as URLs.
- Responda APENAS com um array JSON válido (de [ a ]), SEM cercas, SEM texto extra.

TÓPICOS (visão do PROFESSOR):
1. Banco de questões — criar/organizar categorias, tipos de questão (múltipla escolha, V/F, dissertação, associação, numérica, etc.), importar/exportar questões. (base: /en/Question_bank)
2. Criar e configurar um Questionário (Quiz) — adicionar o Quiz, configurações (tempo, tentativas, método de avaliação, comportamento das questões), adicionar questões do banco/aleatórias, pré-visualizar. (base: /en/Building_Quiz e /en/Quiz_settings)
3. Corrigir tarefas (Assignment) — ver envios, dar nota e feedback, anotar PDF, feedback em vídeo/áudio/arquivo, avaliação em lote, liberar notas. (base: /en/Assignment_activity)
4. Configurar o Relatório de Notas (gradebook) — Notas → Configuração, categorias e itens, agregação (média, soma, pesos), escalas e letras, ocultar/calcular, exportar. (base: /en/Grades e /en/Grade_settings)
5. Rubricas e guias de avaliação — métodos de avaliação avançada: criar rubrica e guia de avaliação, aplicar em atividades. (base: /en/Rubrics e /en/Marking_guide)

# Moodle Question Banks Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, this page exists. The title is "Question banks" from MoodleDocs (Moodle 5.2 documentation).

## Overview
A question bank is a dedicated space where instructors can create, preview, and edit questions for use in quizzes and other question-based activities. Questions are organized hierarchically within categories and subcategories.

## Question Bank Types
The documentation describes two distinct varieties:

1. **Course shared banks** - Located in "Course navigation > More > Question banks," these allow reusable questions across multiple courses with collaborative access among all course teachers.

2. **Quiz-specific banks** - Found in "Quiz navigation > Question bank," these are private to individual quizzes and cannot be shared elsewhere.

## Organization & Management
The page mentions that "Within a question bank, questions may be organized into categories and subcategories," but provides minimal implementation details. Users can apply filters by category, type, status, and other criteria to locate specific questions.

## Import/Export
While the documentation references "Import questions" and "Export questions" as related topics with dedicated pages, **this particular article does not detail the mechanics** of importing or exporting. Those processes are covered separately in the documentation hierarchy.

## Additional Features
Teachers can customize column displays, apply quality-assurance comments, and track question usage and modification history.

# Moodle Quiz Building Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page "Building Quiz" exists on MoodleDocs (version 5.2 documentation).

## Key Steps to Build a Quiz:

**Adding the Quiz Activity:**
Start by clicking the Quiz name on your course homepage, then access the editing screen to begin building.

**Adding Questions:**
Teachers can incorporate questions through three methods:

1. **Create New Questions:** Click "Add" then "+ a new question," select your question type, fill in the form, and save.

2. **From Question Bank:** Select "+ from question bank" to reuse existing questions. You can add individual questions via the plus sign or multiple questions by checking boxes.

3. **Random Questions:** Use "+ a random question" to randomly select from your question bank categories. As the documentation states: "different questions will always be chosen for each" attempt, helping prevent cheating when students test simultaneously.

**Previewing:**
Preview individual questions using the magnifying glass icon, or click the "Preview" button to test the entire quiz. The preview functions like a real quiz, displaying grades and feedback.

**After Attempts:**
Once students attempt the quiz, you can modify question grades and edit content carefully to avoid breaking existing attempts—major changes require regrading student submissions.

# Moodle Quiz Settings Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, the page "Quiz settings" exists on MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

## Key Settings Overview

**Timing:** Instructors can set opening/closing dates and specify time limits. The system includes a countdown timer, automatic submission when time expires, and configurable grace periods for submissions.

**Attempts Allowed:** Teachers determine how many times students may retake the quiz. Multiple attempts can support learning, and different grading methods apply when allowed.

**Grading Method:** When multiple attempts are permitted, four options exist: "Highest grade - the final grade is the highest (best) grade in any attempt," average grade, first attempt grade, or last attempt grade only.

**Question Behaviour:** This controls student interaction with each question. Options range from immediate feedback with retry opportunities to deferred feedback (traditional exam format). The documentation notes that "If you want students to get immediate feedback on their response with a chance to try again, if they get it wrong, then select 'Interactive with multiple tries'."

These settings work together to create customized quiz experiences, from formative learning activities to summative assessments.

# Assignment Activity in Moodle - Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, the page exists with the title "Assignment activity" from MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

## Overview
The Assignment activity enables educators to collect student work for evaluation. As stated in the documentation, "Assignments allow students to submit work to their teacher for grading. The work may be text typed online or uploaded files of any type the teacher's device can read."

## Grading and Feedback Features

**Submission Review:** Teachers access submissions through the Grades section, where they can examine student work and provide evaluation.

**Feedback Methods:** The documentation indicates instructors can annotate submissions directly, download files, enter grades, and provide individual feedback comments to learners.

**Grade Recording:** The system supports "simple percentages or custom scales, or more complex rubrics" for assessment.

**Feedback Tracking:** A notable feature logs when students access feedback files, enabling teachers to monitor engagement through course reports.

## Notable Limitations

The provided content does not detail PDF annotation tools, video/audio feedback capabilities, batch grading features, or grade release workflows. These specific functionalities are not discussed in this particular documentation page, though they may be covered in referenced pages like "Assignment settings" or "Using Assignment."

# Moodle Grades/Gradebook Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the exact title "Grades" on MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

## Content Overview

The Grades documentation serves as a comprehensive guide to Moodle's assessment system. The page functions as a navigation hub organized under "Tracking progress" within course management.

**Key Topics Covered:**

The documentation addresses gradebook fundamentals through the "Grader report" described as "the Gradebook or 'Grader report' is where all course grades are collated." It encompasses:

- Gradebook structure and display through Grade settings
- Grade organization via categories and individual grade items
- Letter grades and custom scales for assessment
- Advanced features including rubrics and marking guides
- Grade visibility controls and hiding options
- Data management through import/export functionality
- Grade calculations and penalty systems
- Historical tracking of grade changes

The page also references related progress-tracking tools like competencies, activity completion, badges, and analytics within the broader course management framework.

**Available Resources:** Documentation is available across multiple Moodle versions (5.1, 5.0, 4.5) and in 8+ languages including Catalan, German, French, Spanish, Italian, and Japanese.

# Moodle Grade Settings Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the exact title "Grade settings" in the Moodle 5.2 documentation.

## Content Overview

The documentation covers three primary configuration levels:

**Course Grade Settings**
These determine gradebook appearance for all course participants and are accessed via the Grades tab's dropdown menu.

**Grader Report Preferences**
Teachers can customize their preferences across all courses, such as choosing to display "only active participants or all participants (including suspended users)."

**Site Administration Settings**
Administrators configure defaults affecting all gradebooks. Key options include:
- **Graded Roles** – specifies user types appearing in gradebooks
- **Scales in Aggregation** – "custom scales will have a corresponding value that is assigned based on the number of options"
- **Grade Publishing** – enables importing/exporting via URL without login
- **Recover Grades Default** – automatically recovers grades upon re-enrollment
- **Unlimited Grades** – permits entries exceeding 100%
- **Grade Point Settings** – establishes maximum and default point values

The page also lists 12 grade-related capabilities, ranging from editing and exporting grades to managing advanced grading methods and outcomes.

# Rubrics in Moodle - Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the exact title "Rubrics" on MoodleDocs (Moodle 5.2 documentation).

## What is a Rubric?

Rubrics serve as an advanced grading method for criteria-based assessment. According to the documentation, they consist of "a set of criteria plotted against levels of achievement" with numeric grades assigned to each level. The final grade is calculated by comparing the actual score against the worst and best possible scores.

## Creating a Rubric

To establish a rubric, educators:
1. Access the Rubric editor through the assignment's Advanced grading settings
2. Define criteria and their corresponding achievement levels
3. Assign point values to each level
4. Configure rubric options (like allowing student preview and enabling remarks)
5. Save the definition as either active or draft status

Teachers can modify criterion weightings through point assignments and use the Tab key for efficient navigation during creation.

## Application to Activities

Rubrics are implemented as an advanced grading method specifically within assignments. During grading, instructors select appropriate achievement levels for each criterion, and the system automatically calculates normalized scores as percentages. Students can preview rubrics before submission if this option is enabled, ensuring transparency about assessment standards.

# Marking Guide Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the exact title "Marking guide" on MoodleDocs (version 5.2).

## What It Is
A marking guide is described as "an advanced grading method where a teacher enters a comment per criterion and a mark up to a maximum."

## Creation Process
Teachers create marking guides by:
- Selecting the marking guide option from the grading method dropdown when setting up an assignment
- Naming and describing the guide
- Defining criteria with explanations and maximum marks
- Adding multiple criteria as needed
- Optionally including frequently used comments for efficient grading

## Application
Once created, the marking guide functions as an advanced grading method integrated into assignments. Teachers use it to evaluate student work by entering scores and feedback per criterion. Students can view the guide before submission to understand expectations, and teachers access it through the assignment grading interface to mark submissions systematically.

The guide can be edited, deleted, saved as a template, or duplicated for reuse across assignments.

# Moodle Question Import Formats

Yes, this documentation page exists and is current (last updated November 2, 2025).

## Supported Import Formats

The page lists these question import formats:

- **GIFT** - "Moodle 'proprietary' text format for import and export"
- **Moodle XML** - "Moodle 'proprietary' xml format for import and export"
- **Aiken** - An accessible format for multiple-choice questions
- **Blackboard** - Supports .dat files and zip archives with media
- **Course Test Manager** - From Course Technology
- **Embedded Answers (Cloze)** - Multiple question/answer format
- **H5P** - Interactive content with embedded questions
- **Hot Potatoes** - Freeware export format
- **Missing Word** - For multiple-choice and short-answer questions
- **Word Table Format** - Structured tables from Microsoft Word files

## Where to Access Import/Export

To import questions, access "the Questions link in the course administration and select the import option." The page notes "it is also possible to get to this screen while editing an existing quiz."

For exporting, the documentation references an "Export questions" section within the Managing questions area.

# Moodle Grade Aggregation Strategies

Yes, this documentation page exists. It's from MoodleDocs version 5.2 and covers grade aggregation options in Moodle's gradebook.

## Available Aggregation Strategy Options

The page lists the following aggregation strategies:

1. **Mean of grades** - "sum of all grades divided by the total number of grades"
2. **Weighted mean** - grades multiplied by assigned weights before averaging
3. **Simple weighted mean** - uses each item's maximum grade as its weight
4. **Mean of grades (with extra credits)** - arithmetic mean supporting extra credit multipliers
5. **Median of grades** - middle value when percentages are ordered
6. **Lowest grade** - smallest normalized grade in the category
7. **Highest grade** - largest normalized grade in the category
8. **Mode of grades** - most frequently occurring normalized grade
9. **Natural** - "sum of all grade values, scaled by relative weights"

The page notes that by default, only "Natural" aggregation is available. Administrators must enable other types through Site administration settings to make them accessible in the gradebook dropdown menu.
